title: Rejoice, Believer, in the Lord
description: Rejoice, Believer, in the Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 84, “Perseverance”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Re-joice, be-liev-er, in the Lord Who makes your cause his own; The hope that's built up-on his word, Can ne'er be o-ver-thrown.

lines: Rejoice, believer, in the Lord
Who makes your cause his own;
The hope that's built upon his word,
Can ne'er be overthrown.
Though many foes beset your road,
And feeble is your arm;
Your life is hid with Christ in God
Beyond the reach of harm.
Weak as you are, you shall not faint,
Or fainting shall not die;
Jesus, the strength of every saint,
Will aid you from on high.
Though sometimes unperceived by sense,
Faith sees him always near;
A Guide, a Glory, a Defence,
Then what have you to fear?
As surely as he overcame,
And triumphed once for you;
So surely you, that love his name,
Shall triumph in him too.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
